author: Marcus Fitzsimmons
title: McGhee Tyson Airport considers costs for FlightPlan expansions - NewsBreak
text:
By Marcus Fitzsimmons ,
5 hours ago
The arrival of Southwest at McGhee Tyson is a week away but the airport is looking far beyond March 5.
The Metropolitan Knoxville Airport Authority held a series of committee meetings on Feb. 18 focused on the airport‚Äôs expansion and growth. The board of directors held a workshop to hear plans on financing for the terminal area development program followed by a meeting of the Capital Development Committee prior to the board‚Äôs February meeting.
The first phase of the expansion known as FlightPlan includes several key components. Several of those, such as the new six-story parking garage and the relocation of the glycol tank farm, are already in progress.
By 2030, the airport intends to also add six gates, expand the security checkpoint and expand the energy plant with those not yet started projects carrying an estimated $356.6 million price tag. The Environmental Assessment, required by the EPA, for the expansion began in December 2025 and is expected to be completed by the end of 2026. The design work for the apron expansion and TSA checkpoint is already underway.
The workshop session provided data to the board members concerning the use of various sources including the Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) and the airline agreements as to how they could be applied to finance the FlightPlan in bond scenarios. The workshop was to see the basic plan and the options and intentions for various scenarios. The board will need to approve a specific measures during future meetings to proceed.
The PFC is a charge to passengers by U.S. commercial airports, managed by the FAA, it is collected by the airlines as part of the purchase of a ticket. The PFC is capped at $4.50, which is the rate used by McGhee Tyson. Use of PFC funds requires FAA approval as the monies are intended to support safety, security and capacity projects at the airport collecting the PFC.
The airline agreements are the fees incorporated into the lease agreements with the airlines operating at the airport. They cover items such as the specifics for gate use, ticket counters, operating space, landing and apron fees. McGhee Tyson‚Äôs current agreements were established in 2018 and expired in 2023, they have been extended on a month-to-month basis ever since.
While many of the FlightPlan projects can be covered largely by the PFC income with FAA approval, the concourse expansion, which entails $244.8 million or 69% of the expansion costs, would require additional revenue. The airport intends to have parallel discussion with the airlines during 2026 ‚Äî one on short-term adjustments for all the other components and a second discussion regarding a new long-term airline agreement that would assist in funding the concourse project.
‚ÄúWe are tracking for a March beginning of conversations with the airlines particularly focused on the need to expand the security checkpoint,‚Äù said Patrick Wilson, president of KMAA. We project the majority of that project should be backed by the passenger fees, so that will be good news to the airlines. We will probably still need to issue debt to move forward with the project. ... We don‚Äôt know yet if that‚Äôs like 75% paid for by PFCs or 90%.
‚ÄúThe short answer is that we are planning to really initiate that, start coordinating dates in March, and that‚Äôs within our current agreements. In reference to the new agreements we are also starting that in parallel, but that‚Äôs a much longer process, probably an 18-month process for that.‚Äù
The workshop looked into timelines and using the issuance of bonds to have the cash on hand for payments. The intention being to issue them in amounts on a time frame that would put the funds in hand shortly before need to minimize the time for the funds to sit unused and reduce the costs of the issuance.
‚ÄúWe do at this point, from everything we have seen, expect that we would look to borrow any funds related this in one or more transactions, likely more,‚Äù Lauren Lowe told the board during the presentation. ‚ÄúThat‚Äôs really going to be based on the timing of cash flows for the project. So, to kind of restate earlier, we wouldn‚Äôt want you borrowing for a project and the funds just sit there, and you can‚Äôt really make those dollars go to work.‚Äù
FY 2027: The Capital Development Committee received a draft of the Airport Capital Improvement Plan that includes both Downtown Island and McGhee Tyson for FY 2027. Staff intends to have the final version ready for approval by the committee and the full board in April.
GRANT: During the meeting of the full board the authority was authorized to accept a $22,500,000 grant from the state to be applied to the cost of the parking garage project.
UP NEXT: The MKAA Board of Directors is scheduled to meet at 4 p.m. Wednesday, March 18, at McGhee Tyson. There will tentatively be a workshop regarding the airport concessions contracts prior to that meeting.
